title: Lung Cancer: Targeted Therapy in 2025
content: Lung cancer treatment has changed in the last twenty years since the discovery of EGFR mutations. In this article, we will review the current state of the art for non-small cell lung cancer actionable genomic alterations (AGA). AGA are mostly found in lung adenocarcinomas, a subtype of non-small cell lung cancers. We will focus on current treatment for EGFR mutations, ALK fusions, ROS1 fusions, BRAF V600E mutations, MET exon 14 skipping mutations, RET fusions, KRAS G12C mutations, ERBB2 mutations (also called HER2 mutations) and NTRK fusions. We will also touch on key toxicities associated with these medications. Treatments are mostly available for metastatic stage, but we will also discuss adjuvant therapy for EGFR mutations and ALK fusions as well as stage III post chemoradiotherapy treatment for EGFR lung cancer.
